title: The Three Little Pigs
lesson: Think about materials, learn from what happens, and solve problems together.
fixedEnding: The three pigs are safe together in a strong house, and the wolf leaves unharmed.

houses.intro: The oldest pig is ready to build a little house in a sunny meadow.
houses.question: What material could the oldest pig use for a little house?

introLines.text: The oldest pig is ready to build a little house in a sunny meadow.
I can't wait to build my own little house!

buildLines.text: I'm going to build a house with {material}!

reactionLines.text: Oh! I need another place to stay. I'll go to my brother!

houses.intro: The brothers reach the middle pig's building place beside the forest.
houses.question: What material could the middle pig try for this house?

introLines.text: The brothers reach the middle pig's building place beside the forest.
Come here, brother! Let's try building a house together!

reactionLines.text: Oh dear, we need another home. Let's go to our youngest brother!

houses.intro: The three pigs join the youngest pig and plan a strong house together.
houses.question: What strong material should the pigs use for their last house?

introLines.text: The three pigs join the youngest pig and plan a strong house together.
Let's take our time and join the walls firmly.
And I'll help put them in place!

buildLines.text: Let's join the {material} pieces firmly, one at a time.

reactionLines.text: Our walls held together! We're safe here together.

paper.label: paper
paper.build: The paper walls are light and carefully folded.
paper.event: The wolf blows, and loose paper pieces blow away, leaving gaps in the roof. The house is no longer safe, so the pigs step aside.
paper.predict: The wolf is about to puff at the light paper house. What do you think will happen?
paper.reflect: Loose paper pieces blew away. Why was the house no longer safe?
process: The wolf puffed, and the paper walls fluttered back and forth.
Their loosely joined edges came free.

setupLines.text: Hee hee! I'll give those walls a great big puff!

eventLines.text: Whoosh! Loose paper pieces blew away from the roof!

straw.label: straw
straw.build: The straw walls are light bundles tied together.
straw.event: The wolf blows, and loose pieces of straw from the roof blow away. The house is no longer safe, so the pigs step aside.
straw.predict: The wolf is about to puff at the light straw house. What do you think will happen?
straw.reflect: Loose straw blew away. Why was the house no longer safe?
process: The wolf puffed, and the straw walls shook.
Loose bits of straw started to come apart.

setupLines.text: Hee hee! I'll give those walls a great big puff!

eventLines.text: Whoosh! Loose straw pieces blew away from the roof!

wood.label: wood
wood.build: The pig stacks wooden logs loosely, leaving the joints unfastened.
wood.event: The wolf's puff shakes the loosely stacked wood. The walls tumble down, and the pigs step safely away.
wood.predict: The wooden logs are loosely stacked. What might happen to the wood house when the wolf puffs?
wood.reflect: The loosely stacked wood house tumbled down. What did we notice about its loose joints?
process: The wolf puffed, and the loosely stacked wood wobbled.
The logs slipped apart because they were not fastened together.

setupLines.text: Ho ho! Let's see what my puff can do!

eventLines.text: Oh! Those loose pieces came apart!

cookie.label: cookie
cookie.build: The pig makes cookie walls. The hungry wolf notices their sweet smell.
cookie.event: The wolf nibbles the cookie walls until the house cannot shelter the pigs. The pigs walk safely to the next building place.
cookie.predict: The hungry wolf smells the cookie walls. What do you think he might do with the cookie house?
cookie.reflect: The wolf ate the cookie walls while the pigs stayed safe. What did we notice about food used for walls?
process: The hungry wolf sniffed the cookie walls.
He took little nibbles, leaving bigger and bigger gaps.

setupLines.text: Sniff, sniff! Those walls smell like a snack!

eventLines.text: Munch, munch! Now there are gaps in the walls!

icecream.label: ice cream
icecream.build: The pig shapes an ice cream house under the warm sun.
icecream.event: The warm sun melts the ice cream walls into a puddle. The pigs stay safe and look for a stronger home.
icecream.predict: The warm sun shines on the ice cream house. What do you think will happen to the ice cream?
icecream.reflect: The ice cream walls melted in the warm sun. What did we notice about ice cream in warm sunshine?
process: In the warm sunshine, drops dripped down the ice cream walls.
The walls grew thinner and softer.

setupLines.text: The warm sun shines down on the walls.

eventLines.text: The pigs watch from a safe place.

brick.label: brick
brick.build: The pigs help one another firmly join the heavy bricks, one by one.
brick.event: The wolf blows at the firmly joined brick house, but it stays standing. All three pigs are safe inside.
brick.predict: The brick walls are heavy and firmly joined. What do you think will happen when the wolf puffs at the brick house?
brick.reflect: The firmly joined brick house stayed standing. How did strong materials and working together help the pigs?
process: The wolf puffed hard at the brick walls.
The firmly joined bricks held one another in place.

setupLines.text: I'll try my biggest puff this time!

eventLines.text: Phew! The walls are still standing!

stone.label: stone
stone.build: The pigs help one another firmly join the heavy stones, one by one.
stone.event: The wolf blows at the firmly joined stone house, but it stays standing. All three pigs are safe inside.
stone.predict: The stone walls are heavy and firmly joined. What do you think will happen when the wolf puffs at the stone house?
stone.reflect: The firmly joined stone house stayed standing. How did strong materials and working together help the pigs?
process: The wolf puffed hard at the stone walls.
The firmly joined stones held one another in place.

setupLines.text: I'll try my biggest puff this time!

eventLines.text: Phew! The walls are still standing!

endingLines.text: Phew, that house is too strong for my puff. I'm heading home!
The wolf walks away unharmed. The three pigs stay safe together.
Thank you for helping me! Next time I'll join the walls firmly.
We thought carefully and helped each other. There is room for everyone!
The three little pigs share their safe home. The End.

narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.speechStyle: Clear, short sentences. Invite the child to notice what happens without grading their answer.
narrator.imageNotes: Describe approved actions and visible changes; do not add a visible narrator to the picture.

pig1.name: The oldest pig
pig1.speechStyle: Lively first-person sentences; eager before building, surprised after an event, comfortable asking for help.
pig1.imageNotes: Show eagerness or surprise with posture and expression. Preserve the existing oldest-pig reference appearance.

pig2.name: The middle pig
pig2.speechStyle: Bouncy, friendly first-person sentences. Welcome a brother and offer to try together.
pig2.imageNotes: Use welcoming gestures and expressive reactions. Preserve the existing middle-pig reference appearance.

pig3.name: The youngest pig
pig3.speechStyle: Calm, practical sentences. Say what to do together, using familiar words instead of construction jargon.
pig3.imageNotes: Show careful work and reassuring gestures. Preserve the existing youngest-pig reference appearance.

wolf.name: Wolf
wolf.speechStyle: Playful, short boasts and gentle huffing sounds. Sound surprised when the house stands; never threaten to eat or hurt the pigs.
wolf.imageNotes: A storybook wolf with comic expressions. Preserve the existing wolf reference; no frightening close-ups or injuries.

fields.speakerId: A fixedCharacters ID; never a display name.
fields.text: Only words to speak, without speaker labels or acting directions.
fields.kind: narration for narrator; dialogue for a character.
fields.tone: Delivery style; stable code independent of language.
fields.emotion: Feeling in this moment; stable code independent of language.

templateVariables.material: Replace with the server-approved material label in the active language, including approved custom materials.

consumers.speech: Use text as the transcript and speakerId as the voice identity; tone/emotion are conditioning labels, never spoken text. Templates are not recordings or training audio.
consumers.storyAgent: Preserve the characters, their personalities, selected material, fixed events and safe ending. Keep setup before the prediction and process before the result.
consumers.image: Use approved scene facts and character references. Personality, imageNotes and line emotion can inform expression; do not render dialogue or directions as text in the picture.
